- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tamil has a unique phonological system with a large number of consonants, including retroflex consonants not found in other Dravidian languages.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tamil has a complex system of vowel length that has developed independently from other Dravidian languages.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tamil has a highly agglutinative morphology, allowing for the formation of long and complex words by adding suffixes to root words.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tamil follows a subject-object-verb (SOV) order, whereas other Dravidian languages mostly follow a subject-verb-object (SVO) order.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tamil has borrowed many words from Sanskrit, influencing its vocabulary, unlike other Dravidian languages.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tamil uses a unique script different from other Dravidian scripts, with a large number of letters representing different sounds.
